reported_value: ~1/3 of 38 monitored NEP blue whales vocalised (13/38); tags: 22% of deployments, 50% of males vs 5% of females; non-vocal whales often feeding >50 m
proposed_distribution: each animal present is vocal with p = 0.33 (male-biased; song only from males)
source: Oleson et al. 2007 MEPS; Lewis et al. 2018

context: Song (AB, Z, SEP, NZ, NWP songs)
reported_value: singers solitary, not paired while singing; other whales sometimes within a few km; McDonald 2001: 3 A-B callers tracked simultaneously in one encounter
proposed_distribution: 1 singer (p 0.7), 2 (0.2), 3 (0.1); extra singers independent, different ranges
source: Oleson 2007 MEPS; McDonald et al. 2001 JASA

reported_value: 3-10 AB units per dive; song call rate 43.3+-4.5 calls/h; A-B 47.8+-3.7 s, B-A 83.0+-25.1 s (tags: A-B 49+-10, B-B 51+-14, B-A 70+-29)
proposed_distribution: units per dive ~ uniform 3-10; phrase intervals from population rows with individual means (below)

reported_value: Antarctic long intervals 172+-48 s (n=44); NZ surfacing gaps median 220 s (109-477, n=28), dive ~727 s; NEP male dive intervals 14-17 min with 4-5 breaths; call pauses match surfacings
proposed_distribution: dive (calling) period ~ N(12, 3) min; surfacing silence ~ lognormal median 200 s (range ~100-480 s)

reported_value: songs 'for many hours at a time' (hours to days); singers monitored 0.8-8 h; one male 5 h 25 min; NZ encounters 4 h 25 min and ~7 h with gaps >10 min
proposed_distribution: song bout ~ lognormal median 3 h (0.5-12 h); silent spells between bouts ~ lognormal median 20 min (assumed)

reported_value: 2-3 whales, always with another blue whale within ~1 km; 3.9+-3.3 calls/h; B-A 983.5+-743.5 s; single A, B or AB pair per dive
proposed_distribution: group 2-3, 1 caller; rate ~ gamma(mean 4, sd 3.3)/h; one call or AB pair per dive
notes: one whale switched from singular calls to song after leaving its partner

reported_value: 1+ whales, others within 1 km; 4.0+-3.7 calls/h; up to 15 D calls per dive; irregular; used as counter-calls among several whales; D-D 835+-1097 s
proposed_distribution: 1-4 callers; rate ~ gamma(mean 4, sd 3.7)/h per caller, clustered within dives (up to 15)

reported_value: NZ 21 Dec encounter switched several times between song and shorter downswept calls; NEP whale switched singular -> song
proposed_distribution: EQUAL number of encounters per context: song-only, D/feeding-only, song + D (switching), singular AB (NEP only); no prior weighting

reported_value: NZ one whale: song repeat 115.2+-0.9 s (n=115) vs population medians 115-133 s; NEP A calls 19-23 pulses (one whale) vs 5-6 (another); 90 Hz component shift differs between individuals
proposed_distribution: per caller: draw individual mean from population distribution; within-caller SD = 0.3 x population SD (assumed)

reported_value: calls identifiable at ~250 km in deep water (less on shelf); SEP songs SNR 1-40 dB; 3rd harmonic 0-16 dB below fundamental (propagation)
proposed_distribution: range/SNR is NOT a feature: caller range ~ log-uniform 1-200 km sets detectability only -> fraction of each contour detected, number of fragments, missing quiet units (e.g. Z-call B/C) and harmonics (0-16 dB below fundamental), frequency jitter; drifts over the encounter as the caller approaches/departs
source: Sirovic 2004 via McDonald 2006 NZ; Malige 2020; McDonald 2001

reported_value: Antarctic: spectral peak of distant Z-calls (28 Hz, 19 Hz) present much of the year (Sirovic 2009 spectra); Weddell Sea Z-calls year-round, peak Jan-Apr (Thomisch 2016). NEP B calls Jun-Jan, peak Sep
proposed_distribution: Antarctic encounters: chorus present p = 0.6 (Feb-Jul) / 0.3 otherwise; NEP p = 0.3 (Aug-Nov) (assumed); chorus = 10-50 callers at SNR -5 to +5 dB, only fragments of loudest units survive

reported_value: NEP B calls Jun-Jan (peak Sep), D calls until ~Nov; SEP2 >90% of SEP song detections; Antarctic year-round, peak Jan-Apr
proposed_distribution: season drawn per encounter; sets context weights and chorus probability
source: Sirovic 2015 ESR; Oleson 2007 AB; Buchan 2015 MMS
